text:
Alana: Pushed nvprof + Nsight capture from nightly perf run. High-level: big idle gap before NCCL all-reduce on TP shards. nvprof summary pasted below, plus repro command.

Alana: nvprof snapshot:
```
GPU activities:
  - kernel: forward_block  55ms
  - kernel: attn_qk       12ms
  - nccl: allreduce      110ms  <-- large
  - kernel: ff_block      48ms
Total step: 280ms
Allreduce ~39% of step on TP2 (seq=2048, bs=8)
```

Alana: Repro command I used:
```
REPRO_CMD="python -m runtime.trace --model redwood-small --tp 2 --bs 8 --seq 2048 --iters 200 --capture nsight"
$REPRO_CMD
```

Matt: Which hardware? 8xA100 or 4xH100?

Alana: 4xH100 on perf-hpc1.

Cheng: Two quick thoughts: 1) KV-cache warmup/prefetch can make per-replica work uneven, 2) kernel selector falling back to a slower kernel on some ranks causes sync stalls at all-reduce.

Sophie: @Alana can you paste the nsight timeline snippet or at least event ordering? Want to see if compute finishes at different times per GPU.

Alana: Timeline summary: compute blocks finish staggered; one replica does a long memcpy then waits. Order: compute -> memcpy (120ms) -> nccl allreduce -> continue. The memcpy looks like a KV cache prefetch.

perf-bot: perf-bot: regression detector: nightly vs baseline (v1.9.3) shows p50 step latency +12% for tp=2/bs=8/seq=2048. Regression flagged 2026-02-18.

Alana: Added micro-timers to runtime to isolate phases:
```
TIMERS:
  kv_prefetch:  ms
  compute_forward: ms
  nccl_allreduce: ms
```
Logs (noisy run):
```
replica0: kv_prefetch=15 compute_forward=80 nccl_allreduce=42
replica1: kv_prefetch=118 compute_forward=78 nccl_allreduce=120
replica2: kv_prefetch=12 compute_forward=81 nccl_allreduce=45
replica3: kv_prefetch=10 compute_forward=83 nccl_allreduce=47
```

Alana: Replica1 doing heavy kv_prefetch => longer nccl wait. Explains the gap.

Matt: Why does replica1 prefetch more? Uneven batch splitting/padding across microbatches? Are we using continuous batching heuristics?

Cheng: Continuous batching pads to longest seq in the microbatch. If token-length skew exists across replicas some replicas do extra prefetch. Also kernel selection: replica1 might have hit a fallback kernel (e.g., attn_qk_generic_fp16) causing different memcpy patterns.

Sophie: I can run two quick experiments on perf-hpc1:
  - Force kernel selector to fast path: export REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=fast_fp16
  - Disable async kv prefetch: export REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0
Will run independently and combined with nsight capture.

Cheng: Run nccl microbench too to rule out NIC issues:
```
/path/to/nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 8M -f 2 -g 4
```
If allreduce latency looks normal, imbalance is likely the culprit.

Alana: Plan: 1) baseline capture, 2) kernel-forced capture, 3) kv-prefetch disabled, 4) both forced. Will attach captures. Also saw kernel selection log: replica1 selected attn_qk_generic_fp16 vs others using attn_qk_optimized_fp16.

Matt: That fits. Slower kernel => longer compute + memcpy => others wait at nccl.

Sophie: If experiments confirm, action items:
  - Add runtime env to prefer consistent kernel across replicas (REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL)
  - Add Console metrics: per-replica nccl_wait_ms and kv_prefetch_ms
  - Add alert: route-level perf regression when nccl_wait_ms p95 increases >10%

Cheng: Also consider tuning continuous batching: optional per-microbatch normalization to cap per-replica padding variance. Small memory cost but reduces stragglers.

Alana: Results: nccl-tests show normal latencies. Kernel-forced run removed the big memcpy; all replicas finished compute within ~5ms and nccl_allreduce dropped to ~48ms uniformly. Disabling kv-prefetch also removed the memcpy. So two orthogonal causes: (A) kernel fallback on some ranks, (B) async kv prefetch creating memcpy stalls on unlucky ranks.

Alana: Patch ideas:
```
- Add env REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL to set kernel family per model shard
- Add runtime metric hooks: metric.nccl_wait_ms[tag=replica]
- Change default: disable async kv prefetch for tp>1 until per-replica throttling exists
```

Matt: Open a short PR with metric + kernel env in runtime repo. Tag me and @Cheng. Keep default off for forced kernel.

Alana: Will do. I'll include nsight capture and nvprof dump in the PR. Filing issue + PR now, will post links when ready.

Cheng: If PR lands, roll canary to 10% of Dedicated clusters first.

Sophie: Add a small nightly eval job to run perf harness and catch this earlier.

Matt: ack.

Alana: Thanks for the triage :thumbsup:
